context: Pointe class and Discovering Repertoire — rises, poses at barre, pointe pirouettes (en dehors and en dedans), soutenus, chaînes, adage

corrections.text: Rises: roll all the way through demi-pointe to a clear ¾ pointe, pressing the toes into the shank rather than arriving passively
Pose en arrière: step in with more confidence, working leg needs to fondu and push off faster
Pose to arabesque: arrive in one count, not a gradual build
Petite coupé: position is below the calf and above the ankle
Arabesque fondu: build tension and length before snapping into the pas de bourrée to full-height retiré — don't collapse into the fondu
Pirouette en dehors from fifth on pointe: weight over the working retiré leg should be close to 60% before push-off, not jumped onto relevé
Pirouette en dehors: turnout momentum should come from the deep hip rotators, not muscled through
Pirouette en dehors: support the arms from the back, not the shoulders
Pirouette en dehors turning left: right side back must snap inward so shoulders and hips square together
Pirouette en dehors: more weight forward overall
Pirouette en dedans on pointe: faster relevé
Pirouette en dedans: relevé foot should scoop under the body into retiré, not swing wide around
Pirouette en dedans: right side back weak and lacking strength — same side as the en dehors turning-left correction
Pirouette en dedans: left foot unstable on pointe specifically in this turn — stable in regular retiré passé, so the instability is turn-specific, not a base retiré problem
Soutenu: weight forward, don't jump onto pointe — it's a spring and snatch, not a jump
Discovering repertoire — chaînes: rhythm not clean, should read as two distinct actions — half-turn, half-turn
Discovering repertoire — chaînes: heels need to stay close, ankles touching in first, weight forward
Discovering repertoire — chaînes: faster spot, hold core — currently leaning back
Discovering repertoire poses: fine overall, could get around faster using the back and spot better
Discovering repertoire poses: don't sickle the foot in retiré
Discovering repertoire: close in tight fifth when finishing the exercise
Discovering repertoire: lift the eyeline up and over when finishing
Discovering repertoire adage: relevé lent and battement need to be much higher — currently well below active capacity

homeExercises.name: Leg on barre in second — active extension protocol
homeExercises.notes: Plié with leg on barre, then relevé with leg on barre, then lift the leg off the barre using the hamstring (not momentum) — repeat holding the leg to the side. Go slowly; the discomfort at end range is the point. This builds active height for relevé lent/battement in the Discovering Rep adage, distinguishing active flexibility from passive, momentum-assisted extension.

openQuestions: Pirouette en dedans: ask for a physical drill or cue to feel the retiré foot 'scooping under the body' rather than swinging wide — currently can't isolate this sensation
Right side back weakness is showing up in both en dehors (turning left) and en dedans pirouettes on pointe — is this recognised as a strength gap that needs targeted conditioning outside class?
